mediums: Two separate gates guard order creation. POST /api/wallet/order is closed unless WALLET_COMMERCE_OPEN is exactly 'true'. The older POST /api/ai/credits/order is gated only by CAPABILITIES.aiTopUps (RELEASE_GATES.aiCommerce). That flag is false in data/capabilities.js (line 8: runtimeAi true, aiCommerce false), and the legacy route also rejects retired packs, so no order can be created today. If someone later flips aiCommerce to true, that route sells the new packs while WALLET_COMMERCE_OPEN is still closed. WALLET-RAZORPAY.md section 4 documents this. Before opening commerce, either make the legacy route honour walletCommerceOpen() or remove it.

Both verify routes (walletCheckout.verifyWalletPayment and api/ai/credits/verify) set the payment row to status 'failed' on a bad signature or a mismatched amount, before checking whether the order was already captured. A user replaying a bad signature against their own already-granted order flips their payment row to 'failed'. No double grant results, because the grant key ai_topup:<orderId>:<paymentId> is idempotent in the database. The row's status would be wrong, though. This predates the branch. Guard it by not downgrading a row that is already 'captured'.

Only the live /wallet page was not run end to end. It was checked on /preview/arena?view=wallet fixtures, so the real Razorpay checkout, a real signature and a real grant were not exercised. The tests cover these steps with injected dependencies, and the docs section 6 test plan covers the rest. A real test-card run on a preview deploy must happen before WALLET_COMMERCE_OPEN is set to true.

In the preview fixture the shell's top-bar credit chip reads 40 while the wallet page says 108. This comes from the preview shell, not the wallet code, so it is cosmetic. It is a trap for anyone reading screenshots.
